name: SyncScribe
description: SyncScribe: real-time collaborative editor with Yjs, a self-hosted Hocuspocus server, GitHub sign-in, server-enforced owner/editor/viewer roles and version history. Live demo runs fully in your browser.

paragraphs: A real-time collaborative document editor with role-based sharing, version history and a self-hosted Yjs sync server.
Live demo: shashank11yadav.github.io/SyncScribe. This is the in-browser demo: it runs entirely in your browser and syncs between your own tabs, with no server behind it.
Two tabs of the GitHub Pages build editing the same document. Captured from the production build with apps/demo/e2e/readme-media.spec.ts.
features: Live co-editing. Yjs merges concurrent edits character by character. Remote cursors show each person's name, and a presence list shows who is in the document.
Owner, editor and viewer roles. Checked on every server action and route handler, and again by the sync server, which gives viewers a read-only socket.
Sharing by email. Works the same whether or not the address has an account yet, so the share dialog cannot be used to find out who has signed up.
Live revocation. Removing someone or lowering their role closes their socket within a second; their next connection gets the new permissions.
Version history. Snapshots are taken while people write. Any version can be previewed and restored, and a restore never destroys the text it replaces.

whatItDoes.text: A real-time collaborative document editor with role-based sharing, version history and a self-hosted Yjs sync server.

requirements.text: GitHub Pages serves static files only, so the live demo cannot run the database, the sign-in flow or the sync server.
GitHub sign-in through Auth.js, with database sessions.
